data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism assumes that a 44-comparator 13-input sorting network must embed a 39-comparator 12-input sorting network as a contiguous prefix. However, sorting networks do not require their prefixes to optimally sort any subset of inputs; a 13-input network of 44 comparators might never sort any 12-input subset until the final comparators. Therefore, demonstrating that no optimal 12-input prefix can be extended with 5 comparators only proves this specific construction method fails, not that 44-comparator networks do not exist or that the search 'stalls at 45'. The target's own countercondition acknowledges a 44-comparator network might not embed an optimal 12-input prefix, invalidating the premise that testing such prefixes meaningfully constrains the search space.
